title: Cells of the Blood
page_title: Cells of the Blood | Cambridge (CIE) AS Biology Revision Notes 2023

blocks.name: Cells of the Blood
blocks.definition: recognise and draw red blood cells, monocytes, neutrophils and lymphocytes from microscope slides, photomicrographs and electron micrographs

blocks.md:
- Blood is a tissue composed of a number of important specialised cells, including:

  - Red blood cells
  - Monocytes
  - Neutrophils
  - Lymphocytes
- These cells all have distinguishable structures which enable them to be recognised on microscope slides, in photomicrographs and in electron micrographs

blocks.alt: Diagram of a red blood cell showing biconcave disc shape, membrane, and haemoglobin. Size is 7.5 µm with no nucleus for more haemoglobin.
blocks.caption: Diagram of the structure of a red blood cell

blocks.md:
- **Red blood cells **contain **haemoglobin**

  - This is a protein with a **quaternary structure** that contains haem iron groups which can bind reversibly to oxygen
- Distinctive features of red blood cells when viewed under a microscope, are their distinctive biconcave disc shape (caused by their lack of nucleus)

blocks.alt: Illustration showing a collection of pink and purple circular shapes resembling a microscopic view of red blood cells, scattered on a white background.
blocks.caption: Red blood cell micrograph

blocks.alt: Diagram of a monocyte with labelled parts: nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondrion, chromatin, Golgi apparatus, lysosome; diameter 18 μm.
blocks.caption: A monocyte is a type of white blood cell

blocks.md:
- **Monocytes** are identifiable by their size

  - They are the largest of the *leukocytes* and have a nucleus shaped like a kidney or a bean
- The nucleus of monocytes tends to appear lighter after staining than other leukocytes
- The nucleus should appear a light blue colour, while the chromatin inside is distinct and fine

blocks.alt: Micrograph of a purple-stained monocyte in a blood smear, showing a large kidney-shaped nucleus and non-granular cytoplasm, surrounded by red blood cells.
blocks.caption: A micrograph of a monocyte cell

blocks.md:
- **Neutrophils** are distinguished by their multi-lobed nuclei
- Up to 70% of all leukocytes are neutrophils

  - This makes them easy to spot on a micrograph
- The granules of neutrophils typically stain pink or purple-blue

blocks.alt: Diagram of a neutrophil cell with labels for multilobed nucleus, glycogen, azurophilic granules, secondary granule, phagosome; diameter 12-14 µm.
blocks.caption: A neutrophil is a type of white blood cell
A micrograph of a neutrophil cell

blocks.md:
- **Lymphocytes** are small leukocytes that are identifiable by their very large nuclei, which typically stains a dark colour
- Lymphocytes constitute around 20-25% of all leukocytes
- Lymphocytes are around the size of red blood cells

blocks.alt: Diagram of a lymphocyte with labels: endoplasmic reticulum, ribosome, cytoplasm, mitochondrion, large round nucleus; diameter 7-14 micrometres.
blocks.caption: A lymphocyte is a type of white blood cell

blocks.alt: A micrograph of some lymphocyte cells
blocks.caption: A micrograph of some lymphocyte cells

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: When looking at micrographs, ensure you distinguish between the kidney-shaped nucleus of a monocyte and the multi-lobed nucleus of a neutrophil, as these can appear similar at first. As with all things, practice is key here!
